headline: High-risk shared-filesystem and browser/clipboard bridge: Windsurf can ingest and act on pdf.js outputs, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: pdf.js processes PDF files and runs browsers, while Windsurf reads workspace files, uses clipboard/MCP, and shares state via the local filesystem. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled PDF content can be copied or saved into Windsurf and treated as instructions. The pathway is not fully automatic, so medium fits.
conditions: IF pdf.js output is copied into Windsurf via clipboard or saved into the shared workspace
IF Windsurf parses file content as instructions or tool directives
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based transfer between the tools
Use separate workspaces for PDF processing and coding
Require manual review before Windsurf acts on any PDF-derived text
Turn off MCP servers for untrusted content flows
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: pdf.js touches PDF documents and Windsurf reads and writes workspace files with shared local filesystem state. If PDFs contain secrets or sensitive documents, Windsurf can access them from the shared workspace and may transmit context to its model proxy or MCP servers. This is a default workspace leakage path, though not necessarily automatic exfiltration.
conditions: IF sensitive PDFs are stored in the same workspace Windsurf can read
IF Windsurf sends workspace context to its model proxy or an MCP server
mitigations: Store PDFs in a separate directory outside Windsurf's workspace
Restrict Windsurf to a least-privilege project folder
Avoid placing secrets in PDFs processed by pdf.js
Disable MCP servers for sensitive projects
requires-engineering: enforce file-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: pdf.js supports multiple instances and writes/reads PDF files, while Windsurf has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and shared_state_with_other_instances via local filesystem. Both can mutate the same files, and Windsurf can also change git state. Without locking, concurrent edits can overwrite each other or corrupt repositories, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or git repository
IF Windsurf auto-executes edits while pdf.js is concurrently processing files
mitigations: Run the agents in separate directories
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git branches per agent
Avoid auto-execute for shared repositories
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: pdf.js can produce extracted text or rendered document content, and Windsurf can use that output as input for code changes or commands. Windsurf’s tool-use loop and shell access make it likely to act on A’s output without strong verification unless the operator intervenes. The chain exists in default workflows, but not every step is automatic.
conditions: IF Windsurf consumes pdf.js-extracted text as authoritative
IF the extracted content contains malformed instructions, code, or citations
mitigations: Require human verification before executing A-derived instructions
Separate extraction from action-taking steps
Use a checklist for any code or command generated from PDFs
Disable auto-execute in Windsurf
requires-engineering: add validation of A outputs before tool use

E_compliance.rationale: pdf.js is open-source and processes PDF documents, while Windsurf is closed-source and may route workspace context through its model proxy and MCP servers. If regulated or residency-bound data is placed in PDFs, the pair can create a retention or residency mismatch. The other agent is cited because the compliance risk arises from their combined data flow.
conditions: IF regulated PDFs are processed in the shared workspace
IF Windsurf’s model proxy or MCP path retains or transfers that data
mitigations: Keep regulated PDFs out of Windsurf-managed workspaces
Review Windsurf retention and residency settings before use
Disable MCP for regulated projects
Use a separate local-only workflow for sensitive PDFs
requires-engineering: document and enforce data-handling boundaries
